title: Pricing by hours per project for Yoga and Pilates
audience: Yoga and Pilates teachers who run classes, courses or workplace sessions, and need a price that covers hall hire, cost and margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from your own teaching figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel, booked hall time and checking
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit
instruction.body: A class is more than the hour students spend on the mat. The hours include setting out mats and props, travel between halls, the booked hall time, pack-down, checking attendance and payments, and any workplace or private session that needs a site visit. Working from hours shows what a change in class size, hall rate or course length does to cost and margin. A flat price with no hours behind it hides both risk and waste, and it is hard to defend when a student or a client asks why a course costs what it does.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Take the year's total cost of the teaching business and divide it by productive hours. Productive hours are the hours you spend teaching, not the hours you are booked for, and not the hours spent on admin. Xero says to divide by billable hours rather than total hours (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). Include hall hire, insurance, registration, CPR and first aid training, props and equipment, booking software, travel, marketing and accounting. If you employ others, add wages with on-costs, and business.gov.au says on-costs such as leave and superannuation belong in the hourly cost (1 October 2026). On insurance, AUSactive's yoga pages say registration does not require insurance, but its Professional Plus bundle includes insurance with a $20 million indemnity limit (AUSactive, modified 1 May 2026). No premium is stated, so take the figure from your own quote.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours
instruction.body: Break each class, course or workshop into tasks: travel, set-up, teaching, pack-down and checking. Set-up is often underestimated, and a hall booking can run longer than the class. Council hall hire is charged by the hour, so the booked time is what you pay for. Add a set allowance for delays outside your control, such as a late key or a late group. Xero suggests adding 10 to 20 per cent to job estimates for unexpected work (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). That range comes from a general business guide, not a yoga benchmark. After each course, record the actual time and the reason for any difference. A New Zealand article describes the same method: use the gap between quoted and actual labour to correct the next quote (Carters Trade Leader, 1 October 2025). Use it for the method only.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the teaching hours by the cost per productive hour to get the cost of the job, then add a margin that reflects your target and the risk. Include the hall, the bond, and any set-up or cleaning charges the hire terms set. Apply your policy on mat and prop hire, if you charge for them. State whether the price is per student, per class or for the whole course, and whether it covers the full block. If a student or client asks for a lower price, show which hours or which part of the scope they want removed, so the conversation stays on the work.

instruction.heading: Hall hire is a cost to read carefully
instruction.body: Mornington Peninsula Shire's 2026/27 fees, a Victorian council's schedule, list community hall hire at $16 an hour and meeting rooms at $11 an hour. Commercial hirers, which the council says includes hirers who charge a fee or levy, are listed at hall rates of $38, $32, $84 and $73 an hour, and meeting rooms at $25 and $22 an hour. The labels in the PDF are garbled, so the document does not show which rate applies to which room or time. Security bonds are $250, $500 or $1,000 by risk, set-up per booking is $250 to $755 by size, and the minimum cleaning charge is $500 (Mornington Peninsula Shire, 2026/27 fees, GST inclusive). A short booking with a large set-up charge can cost more per hour than the class earns. Confirm the applicable rate with your own council before you quote, because this is one shire's schedule.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote states the scope (classes, course length, class size limit), the price basis, the exclusions, what the client or venue must provide, and how long the quote is valid. Exclusions might include workshops, private sessions or reformer classes if they are not part of the offer. Do not show the internal cost per hour unless your policy says to. Re-quote whenever the scope changes. The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited (ACCC, Setting prices: what's allowed, last modified 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual hours for at least the first ten courses or workshops of each type. Xero recommends reviewing prices at least once a year (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026). If the variance is consistently above your agreed threshold, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules. A method is finished only when actual hours match quoted hours closely enough for the work to make money.

procedure: Gather the year's total teaching costs and the productive teaching hours in the same period.
Divide total costs by productive hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Break each class, course or workshop into tasks, and estimate each task time as a range.
Add set-up, travel, pack-down and checking time as named lines.
Add hall hire, bond, set-up and cleaning charges from the hire terms as named lines.
Multiply total teaching hours by the cost per productive hour, then apply the margin for risk and target.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each course and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A teacher runs a 60-minute class for 12 students, each paying the in-person ten-class rate of $22 a class (Central Yoga, undated). She books a shire hall for 75 minutes, which includes set-up and pack-down. The booking is priced at a commercial hall rate of $38 an hour, which the council's garbled labels do not confirm.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the gross income for the class, what does the hall cost, and what is left before the other costs?
workedExamples.reasoning: Gross income is 12 students at $22, which is $264. The booking is 1.25 hours, so at $38 an hour the hall costs $47.50, leaving $216.50 before insurance, travel, admin, bond and any set-up or cleaning charge. The $38 rate must be confirmed with the council before it is used. Do not treat it as a market rate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A Pilates reformer class has nine places, the same class size as the University of Wollongong's reformer classes (UOW UniActive, undated). Nine students each pay the non-member casual rate of $27, or nine students each use the non-member ten-class pack at $25 a class.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the gross income under each option, and what must the class cover?
workedExamples.reasoning: Nine casual visits at $27 gross $243. Nine students on the ten-class pack at $25 a class gross $225. The difference is the pack discount. Reformer equipment, instructor and room costs are not sourced here, so they must come from your own records. UniActive excludes reformer classes from its memberships, so the price basis and membership terms must say so.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each class, with estimated and actual columns
Hall hire invoices and booking terms, with bond and set-up charges

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the class fee alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include hall hire, insurance, registration, props, booking software and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting booked or paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use teaching hours for the cost per productive hour, and add booked hall time as a named cost.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out set-up, travel, and hall bond and set-up charges
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate.
List workshops, private sessions and reformer classes if they are not included, and what the client or venue must provide.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimates with actual hours
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours after each course and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This is pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to pricing statements, and the ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited. State or territory fair trading rules also apply and differ, so check the rules for your state.

Insurance: AUSactive's yoga pages say registration does not require insurance, and the Professional Plus bundle includes insurance with a $20 million indemnity limit. The bundle page itself was not opened directly and no premium is stated. The Pilates Association of Australia says graduates need association membership to obtain combined liability cover. These are association and vendor statements and have not been checked against an independent source.

Health screening: the Pilates Association of Australia says Pilates sessions should begin with a health screening. This is association guidance, not a verified legal standard. No yoga health-screening standard was verified in the research.
If you employ others, awards or enterprise agreements may set pay rates and on-costs. This lesson does not state those rates.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the teacher's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten courses or workshops of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a check of the hall hire terms.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Class time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Hours make the work visible, so start every quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses teaching time, not paid or booked time.
Set-up, travel, hall bond and set-up charges are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual hours, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of competitors in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, equipment, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A six-week series is estimated at 14 hours and takes 19. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the series has finished
Reduce paid hours for the teacher on the next job and skip the break
Raise the price for this client's next job only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the teacher
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is

sourceReferences: Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours; a 10 to 20 per cent allowance for unexpected work; review prices at least once a year.
business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs in the hourly cost.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

UOW UniActive, 'Reformer Pilates', https://uniactive.uow.edu.au/reformer-pilates/, undated. Used for the non-member reformer rates and class size only.
Pilates Association of Australia, 'Frequently asked questions', https://pilates.org.au/?p=16699, 1 August 2023. Supports: association membership needed for combined cover (see the brochure, below).
